idea-plugin.name: KubeContext Safety
idea-plugin.description:
KubeContext Safety — Color-Coded Kubernetes Context Guard for Your IDE

One wrong kubectl command in the wrong context can take down production. KubeContext Safety adds a color-coded context indicator to your IDE status bar and requires confirmation before switching to production environments — giving your team a critical safety net.

Context Awareness

  • Status bar widget showing current kubectl context name at all times
  • Color-coded environment indicators: red (production), yellow (staging), green (development)
  • Tooltip with full context details: cluster, namespace, user
  • Automatic kubeconfig monitoring with 2-second polling (multiple KUBECONFIG files are merged like kubectl does)

Safety Features

  • Confirmation dialog before switching to production contexts
  • Balloon notification when the active context becomes a production one (also when changed outside the IDE)
  • 17 built-in rules auto-classify contexts (prod, staging, dev, minikube, kind, k3d, etc.)

Productivity

  • Quick context switch with Ctrl+Shift+K keyboard shortcut
  • Context switch popup listing all available contexts
  • No terminal needed to change kubectl context

Rules

  • Custom context classification rules with pattern matching
  • Team-shared rules via .k8s-guard.yaml in the project root

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2023.2+ (or any JetBrains IDE based on IntelliJ Platform)
  • kubectl on PATH (only needed for switching contexts from the IDE)
  • Valid kubeconfig file (~/.kube/config, KUBECONFIG or a path set in Settings)

Support

  • GitHub: github.com/JirakJ/kubernetes-context-guard
  • Issues: Report a Bug
  • Author: Jakub Jirák
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.8.0

  • The plugin is now completely free — all features unlocked, no license needed.
  • Source code is now open source under Apache-2.0: https://github.com/JirakJ/kubernetes-context-guard

What's New

  • Status Bar Widget - Always see which Kubernetes cluster you are connected to at a glance
  • Color-Coded Environments - Red for production, yellow for staging, green for development contexts
  • Production Guard - Confirmation dialog before switching to any production context
  • Quick Context Switch - Change kubectl context from the IDE without using the terminal
  • 17 Built-in Rules - Auto-classifies contexts by name patterns like prod, staging, dev, minikube, and k3d
  • Kubeconfig Monitoring - File watcher detects external context changes with 2-second polling
  • Team-Shared Rules - Share context classification with your team via .k8s-guard.yaml in your project
  • Custom Context Rules - Define your own pattern-to-environment mappings for any naming convention
